### Responsive breakpoints ignore the app font scale, so compact layouts switch on at the wrong width

* **ID:** f-20260927-08 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-ui · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/components/settings/SettingsPage.tsx:126` (`useMediaQuery("(max-width: 50rem)")`), `src/components/settings/SettingsPage.module.css:60` (`@media (max-width: 50rem)`), and the Mantine `SimpleGrid cols` breakpoints at `src/components/files/FilesPage.tsx:217`, `src/components/databases/DatabasesPage.tsx:185,254`, `src/components/engines/EnginesPage.tsx:133`, `src/components/tabs/NewTabHome.tsx:241`, `src/components/engines/AddEngine.tsx:90,115`, `src/components/databases/AddDatabase.tsx:156`.
* **Defect:** `App.tsx:209` scales the root font (`document.documentElement.style.fontSize = fontSize%`), but `rem`/`em` inside a media query resolve against the initial 16px, never the scaled root. So every breakpoint means the same pixel width at every app font scale: at 200% a 1000px window is only 31 root-em wide, yet Settings stays in its two-column layout (threshold 800px) and the grids stay multi-column, into widths the scaled content cannot fit.
* **Evidence:** root cause 2 of `f-20260829-02` (its 2026-08-31 investigation). That run's 320px matrix never exercises it, because at 320px every breakpoint is already in its narrowest state; the f-20260829-02 plan review (2026-09-27, issue I3, lenses review-plan and review-root-cause) ruled a scale-aware breakpoint outside that finding's mandate because it changes behaviour only at other widths.
* **Fix:** make the compact/column switch follow the effective width in scaled root-em — e.g. derive the query from `fontSizeAtom` (Mantine `useMediaQuery` re-subscribes when its query string changes, measured in `node_modules/@mantine/hooks/esm/.../use-media-query.mjs`), CSS container queries, or content-driven wrapping (`flex-basis` in rem) — and drive the CSS side from the same source.
* **Open question:** one mechanism for all sites (atom-derived pixel query vs. container queries vs. rem flex-basis wrapping), and whether Mantine's theme breakpoints should be rewritten globally or per site.
* **Proof:** an e2e project at e.g. 1000px / 200% font scale whose Settings and a SimpleGrid page pass `assertNothingClipped(page.locator("body"), { scrollable: "reachable" })` and switch to their compact layout.
* **Related:** f-20260829-02 (root cause 2).

Resolved in code commits e4cf2b80, 2345d764 and bad84bf1. One em-scaling function drives Mantine default breakpoints and the shared Settings/Files query hook. App rebuilds the theme when font size changes. Settings' outer compact marker covers tabs and search. Shared compact slider flow space keeps both font and volume marks reachable.

Root proof passed302 phase1 unit tests,168 repair unit tests,96 full pinned-container cases, contract and pre-review gates. ### The release-surface checker keeps its own line-based `#[cfg(test)]` region walker beside the coverage gate's test-only item scanner

* **ID:** f-20260928-02 · **Status:** open · **Area:** gate-scripts · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `scripts/check-rust-release-surface.mjs` (`isTestCfgAttribute`, `walkGatedLines`, `testRegionAtDepth`), and the test-only item scanner `scripts/rust-test-only.mjs` introduced by `f-20260829-04`.
* **Defect:** two scanners now answer "is this Rust code compiled only under `test`?" with different rules. The release-surface walker is line-based: `isTestCfgAttribute` accepts only `cfg(test)` or an `all(…)` whose text contains `test` (so `cfg(not(not(test)))` and `cfg_attr(not(test), cfg(test))` are production to it, and an `all(any(test, windows), unix)` is test-only to it although it is compiled on Windows without `test`), and region ends are tracked by brace depth from the first `{` on a line. The coverage gate's scanner (`f-20260829-04`, `d-20260927-24`) evaluates the predicate three-valued with `test` false and every other atom unknown, handles `cfg_attr`, and bounds item extents by `;`, `,`, closers and brace blocks. Both already share one masker (`scripts/rust-source-mask.mjs`, extracted in `f-20260829-04`). A disagreement means one gate calls production what the other calls test code, and the release-surface R1–R4 verdicts (dead-code allowance, fs surface counts, injection-name exposure) can be wrong on exactly the constructs where they differ.
* **Why deferred:** `f-20260829-04`'s plan review (round 1, `review-minimalism`) found the duplicate masker, which that run extracted; routing the region walker through the new scanner changes another gate's verdicts and its shrink-only counts, which is outside that finding's mandate (the plan-review adoption gate).
* **Related:** `f-20260829-04` (introduced the second scanner), `f-20260830-23` (the release-surface R3/R4 fs surface this walker feeds).
* **Open question:** does `walkGatedLines` become a consumer of `rust-test-only.mjs`'s ranges (one predicate, one extent rule for both gates, with the fs surface counts re-measured), or is a line-granular walker kept deliberately for the release surface — and if kept, which of the two predicates is the authority?

### The coverage ratchet accepts a 0/0 → 0/n drop, which the floors read as 100 % → 0 %

* **ID:** f-20260928-03 · **Status:** open · **Area:** gate-scripts · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` `assertBaseline` (the ratio clause, ~line 478) and `assertAreaFloors` (~line 511).
* **Defect:** `assertAreaFloors` reads a metric with `total = 0` as 100 %, but `assertBaseline` compares ratios by cross-multiplication, so a prior `0/0` against a report `0/1` gives `0*0 < 0*1` = false — no regression. An area metric that had no records and gains an uncovered one passes the ratchet, and with a floor of 0 it passes the floor too, although under the floors' own reading it fell from 100 % to 0 %. Found by `review-correctness` during `f-20260829-04`'s plan review (round 10, confidence 97); that run's writer guard (`--write-baseline`) defines `total = 0` as 100 % and refuses the same drop, so the two paths now disagree.
* **Why deferred:** outside `f-20260829-04`'s mandate (the writer guard, the exclusion, the re-record); changing the ratchet's comparison is a separate change with its own shrink-allowance interplay (`f-20260829-15`).
* **Fix shape:** make `assertBaseline`'s ratio clause treat `total = 0` as ratio 1 on both sides (consistent with `assertAreaFloors` and the writer), check the interaction with the shrink-adjusted baseline, and add the `0/0 → 0/1` case to `scripts/coverage-report-tests.mjs` plus a failure-matrix row.
* **Related:** `f-20260829-04` (writer guard with the 100 % rule), `f-20260829-15` (shrink allowance).

### SQLite opens the authorized database by pathname after the parent-bound probe, so a same-inode parent swap in that window moves `-wal`/`-shm` into the replacement directory

* **ID:** f-20260929-01 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** sqlite-pathname-open · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs` — `acquire_probed` (~`:978-986`: `target.open_current()` probe, then `pool.get()`), pool construction through `sqlite_uri(target.path())` (~`:805`); `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs:183` (`ConnectionOptions` enables WAL).
* **Defect:** since `f-20260912-05` (commit `5953bafd`, `d-20260929-01`) a persisted database entry is bound to its authorized parent directory and `database_file_target` refuses a replacement parent. The repository then probes the carrier (`open_current`, which compares a re-walked parent with the retained, now authenticated one) and drops the probe before the pool opens SQLite by pathname. A parent directory replaced in that window by one holding a hard link to the same database inode passes nothing new — the leaf is the same object — but SQLite derives `x.db3-wal`/`x.db3-shm` from the pathname, so the journal and shared-memory files are created in the replacement directory.
* **Open question:** how does the SQLite open inherit the authenticated parent? Candidates: on unix open through `/proc/self/fd/<retained parent>/<leaf>` so SQLite's sidecar names resolve relative to the held directory (measure that SQLite, diesel 2.1.4 and the `file:` URI with `mode=rw` accept it, and what the Windows analogue is); or re-probe the parent after the connection is established and discard the connection on mismatch (does not stop the sidecar creation itself). `f-20260905-03`'s handled note records the same A-B-A opening window for the leaf and rejected a pathname adapter.
* **Why it matters:** `f-20260912-05` named SQLite `-wal`/`-shm` among the writes the parent binding must keep in the authorized directory; the binding now holds up to the carrier, and this is the remaining pathname hop.
* **Related:** `f-20260912-05` (the parent binding this builds on), `f-20260905-03` (repository re-key; records the pathname-open residual), `f-20260912-07`.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-root-cause` lens, cumulative review of the `f-20260912-05` build run, 2026-09-29 (drain session `6f9c4b3e-8255-48b2-82b2-497c962dd7df`).
* **Scope extended, 2026-09-29 (from `f-20260912-07`, lens `review-pgn-index`, confidence 93):** the same SQLite pathname hop also sits inside the identity probe. `DatabaseRepository::identity_from_probe` interleaves four descriptor probes (`probe_schema` → `open_current`, which refuses any inode but the authority-bound one) with four `read_revision` calls, and `read_revision` (`repository.rs:532-544`) opens `sqlite_uri(target.path(), ReadOnly)` by pathname. A leaf swapped A→B only while each revision is read and restored before the next descriptor probe yields an identity with A's object/length/mtime and B's revision, and the search-index loader then accepts a sidecar built for that mixed identity. Whatever mechanism this finding chooses for SQLite to inherit the authorized object must cover the revision probe's connection as well as the pool (and note the WAL constraint: a `/proc/self/fd/<leaf fd>` open would derive `-wal`/`-shm` from the magic-link name and miss the real WAL, so a read-only revision read through it can return a stale revision — measure before adopting). `d-PENDING` of `f-20260912-07` records that the loader itself needs no post-open re-probe.
<!-- ledger-meta {"command":"annotate","effect_lines":1,"effect_sha256":"e81de20b4bc43669a0f9f41ff109c1a9b37ac0e5f175df78bac3fc4051697f4c","input_sha256":"4a9bdf5464ffa29cf56898a275dc776251b66b04ef12e810bb773e4bea049da1","kind":"mutation-receipt","operation":"d163423846381dfc0bb26866675b8ae9806125fe23ba8fccaa211823d43aaf60","options":{"section":null},"request_id_sha256":null,"results":["f-20260929-01"],"target":"f-20260929-01","v":1} -->

* **Closed, 2026-09-29 (drain session `1af0f1fc-ab06-4981-9a3d-47a89d71c541`, build run):** every SQLite open of an authorized database — the repository pool and the identity probe's `read_revision` — now goes through `db::bound_sqlite` (`d-20260929-04`): SQLite opens a reserved name (`/<chessfable-bound>/<token>/<leaf>`) that load-time hooks on the unix and win32 syscall tables resolve relative to a dup of the retained parent descriptor (no-follow), so `-wal`, `-shm` and `-journal` are created, opened and unlinked only in the authorized parent, even after a same-inode parent swap; a per-binding VFS refuses any other name and super-journal opens. Witnesses (red with the pathname URI restored): pool and revision-read parent swaps with sidecars observed while open and after close, rollback-mode WAL conversion journal, hot-journal recovery through the pool and the read-only probe, Windows reparse sidecar. Commits `9ea21bc0`, `dcf0fb13`, `7512d2dc`, `63d9ad1c`, `7deff8d0`, `e6d9581e`, `2cce8662`, `7d2eb019`, `2a79b922`, `0bf839aa`; decisions `d-20260929-04`, `d-20260929-05`; review record `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-29-sqlite-pathname-open-review.md`. Rejected: `/proc/self/fd` naming (measured: resolved back to a pathname), an `xOpen`-only shim (cannot reach `-shm`), a private snapshot, a shared VFS. ### A non-regular file planted as an authorized database's `-shm` can block SQLite's open inside the identity probe

* **ID:** f-20260929-03 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** SQLite 3.39.2 unix VFS `unixOpenSharedMemory` (`libsqlite3-sys-0.25.2/sqlite3/sqlite3.c:40120-40135`), reached from `DatabaseRepository::read_revision` and the repository pool (`src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs`), after `f-20260929-01`'s binding also through `src-tauri/src/db/bound_sqlite.rs`.
* **Defect:** SQLite opens `<db>-shm` with `O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW` and, if that fails, retries `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW`. Neither carries `O_NONBLOCK`, and SQLite does not check the file type, so a FIFO planted as `-shm` in the authorized directory can block the read-only fallback's `open()` indefinitely (a FIFO opened read-only blocks until a writer appears), hanging the identity probe or a pool worker. Pre-existing with pathname opens; unmeasured (no probe run yet).
* **Why it matters:** a hung native identity probe stalls search/index loading for that database; the actor needs write access to the authorized directory, which is also SQLite's own trust boundary for `-wal`.
* **Open question:** should the bound SQLite hooks refuse non-regular sidecars (open with `O_NONBLOCK`, `fstat` `S_ISREG`, clear `O_NONBLOCK`), and what error does the caller then see — or is an in-parent FIFO inside SQLite's accepted trust boundary and to be documented as a residual? Measure first whether the fallback path is reachable (it requires the `O_RDWR` open to fail).
* **Related:** `f-20260929-01` (the SQLite binding whose plan review surfaced it; withdrawn from that plan as outside its mandate by `review-correctness` and `review-minimalism`, round 3), `f-20260912-07`.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-tauri-security` lens, plan review round 2 of `tasks/plans/2026-09-29-sqlite-bound-vfs.md`, 2026-09-29 (drain session `1af0f1fc-ab06-4981-9a3d-47a89d71c541`).

**Widened 2026-09-30 (cumulative review of the `f-20260929-06` build run, commit `0e2d799b`; Codex `review-pgn-index` 93 and `review-tauri-security` 95):** the same blocking-open shape exists for the **database leaf itself on non-Linux unix**. `src-tauri/src/db/bound_sqlite.rs` `unix_hooks::open_hook_inner` (non-Linux branch) checks the leaf with `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` and then calls `openat(parent, leaf, flags | O_NOFOLLOW)` without `O_NONBLOCK`; a writer that replaces the leaf with a FIFO between the two calls makes a read-only open (`read_revision`, `repository.rs` ~597) block until a FIFO writer appears, before the post-open identity check runs; four such requests can hold every `BLOCKING_GATEWAY` permit. Linux is no longer affected: since `0e2d799b` the leaf is opened `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW` (measured M5 in the f-06 plan: returns at once on a FIFO, `S_ISFIFO` → identity mismatch → `ESTALE`). The design question carries over with one added constraint from `f-20260929-06`: on non-Linux, clearing `O_NONBLOCK` after the open is a fallible step on a lockable descriptor, and the hook must never close a lockable leaf descriptor of a possibly locked inode — so the answer has to say whether `O_NONBLOCK` stays set on the verified regular-file descriptor (no effect on regular-file I/O) or how a failed `F_SETFL` is handled without a close.
<!-- ledger-meta {"command":"annotate","effect_lines":1,"effect_sha256":"af3e3e7c18ddf6c216854ed6b87b5131980fde857f8c35e8a36fd2948773729f","input_sha256":"4d93ab2478e3d71afa415c616da4484cf97c154a8698342ebdefdfa985dedc44","kind":"mutation-receipt","operation":"7d50796a659fc956a3d927727eccca6a02f2bebbaeab3ef3ed5ace93cf440c66","options":{"section":null},"request_id_sha256":null,"results":["f-20260929-03"],"target":"f-20260929-03","v":1} -->

* **Measured implementation update, 2026-10-09 (Codex):** The earlier “unmeasured (no probe run yet)” statement is superseded. ### A failing pooled SQLite open is retried and logged at error level for the full r2d2 timeout without naming the database

* **ID:** f-20260929-04 · **Status:** open · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs` pool construction in `DatabaseRepository::entry` (`Pool::builder()` without `connection_timeout` or `error_handler`), r2d2 0.8.10 `add_connection` retry loop (`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/r2d2-0.8.10/src/lib.rs:219-278`).
* **Defect:** when a pooled connection cannot be established, r2d2 retries on its worker threads with exponential backoff until the default 30 s `connection_timeout`, and its default `LoggingErrorHandler` logs every failed attempt at error level with only Diesel's message ("unable to open database file") — no database identifier. The caller waits 30 s and the native log gains a burst of uncorrelated error lines. Pre-existing for any establish failure; more reachable once `f-20260929-01`'s binding refuses opens of a swapped leaf.
* **Why it matters:** an unattributable log burst and a 30 s stall for a condition that is already known to be permanent after the first refusal.
* **Proposed fix:** give the repository pool a contextual `error_handler` (database path/entry key, deduplicated) and a bounded `connection_timeout` suited to the local file case; prove with a test that a refused open returns promptly and logs once.
* **Related:** `f-20260929-01` (surfaced during its plan review, `review-error-handling` round 7, confidence 89; outside that plan's mandate).
* **Found by:** Codex `review-error-handling` lens, plan review round 7 of `tasks/plans/2026-09-29-sqlite-bound-vfs.md`, 2026-09-29 (drain session `1af0f1fc-ab06-4981-9a3d-47a89d71c541`).

### Two hard-link names of one database in the same directory share SQLite's `-shm` but get separate `-wal` files

* **ID:** f-20260929-05 · **Status:** open · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs` (`hard_link_bindings_have_separate_repository_entries`, `:1795-1815`, pins separate entries for two names of one inode); SQLite 3.39.2 unix VFS per-inode record and `-shm` node keyed by (dev, ino) (`libsqlite3-sys-0.25.2/sqlite3/sqlite3.c:36876-36887, 40068-40112`) while the WAL name is derived from each connection's own path (`:58717-58723`).
* **Defect:** when both names are open in one process, SQLite pairs a single shared-memory wal-index with two different `-wal` files. SQLite documents multiple links to one database file as a corruption hazard. Pre-existing with pathname opens; `f-20260929-01`'s binding keeps both names' sidecars inside the one authorized parent but does not change the pairing.
* **Why it matters:** a user who registers the same database twice through hard-linked names in one folder can corrupt it by opening both.
* **Open question:** refuse a second concurrent name for an inode that already has a live binding in the same directory (a user-visible `Conflict` until the first repository entry is evicted — the entry keeps its binding alive while cached), route both names through one binding (then the binding's leaf name must survive the deletion of either name), or detect hard-linked databases at registration and refuse them?
* **Related:** `f-20260929-01` (plan review round 9 of `tasks/plans/2026-09-29-sqlite-bound-vfs.md`: `review-plan` asked for safe pairing, `review-correctness` showed sharing one binding breaks the surviving alias when the other name is deleted; both left outside that mandate), `f-20260905-03`.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-plan` / `review-correctness` lenses, plan review round 9, 2026-09-29 (drain session `1af0f1fc-ab06-4981-9a3d-47a89d71c541`).

### A refused bound SQLite leaf open can still close a descriptor of a locked foreign inode, or hold descriptors until the inode's binding drops

* **ID:** f-20260929-06 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** sqlite-pathname-open · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/db/bound_sqlite.rs` unix `open` hook (pre-open `fstatat` identity check, `openat`, post-open `fstat` check, `retain_mismatched_descriptor` quarantine with a per-inode cap; the `fstat`-failure branch closes the fresh descriptor).
* **Defect:** the bound open refuses a leaf whose identity is not the authority-bound one. The pre-open `fstatat` check handles the ordinary case without opening, but a writer that swaps the leaf to another bound database B between that check and `openat` produces a real descriptor of B. Closing it would drop every POSIX lock this process holds on B (SQLite's locks are process-associated), so it is quarantined until B's last binding drops — bounded per inode by a cap, beyond which it is closed and the lock hazard returns. The rare `fstat`-failure branch closes an unclassified descriptor unconditionally. Needs a local actor who can write the authorized directory and win the race repeatedly.
* **Why it matters:** a dropped lock lets another process write B while this process's SQLite connection believes it holds a lock (corruption); an uncapped quarantine lets the race exhaust descriptors.
* **Open question:** on Linux, verify the leaf on an `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW` descriptor (whose close skips `locks_remove_posix`, `FMODE_PATH`) and reopen it through `/proc/self/fd/<n>` with SQLite's flags, so a lockable descriptor of a foreign inode is never created — measure that the reopen yields the same inode and that closing an `O_PATH` fd leaves another descriptor's POSIX locks intact; what is the macOS equivalent (none known: no `O_PATH`), and is the documented residual acceptable there?
* **Related:** `f-20260929-01` (the binding this refines; surfaced by `review-pgn-index` and `review-tauri-security` in the cumulative review, 2026-09-29), `f-20260912-07`; FIFO sidecar finding (inbox `20260929-071945-307309-1790659185646737657-3`).
* **Found by:** Codex `review-pgn-index` / `review-tauri-security`, cumulative diff re-review of the `sqlite-pathname-open` build run, 2026-09-29 (drain session `1af0f1fc-ab06-4981-9a3d-47a89d71c541`). Review record: `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-29-sqlite-pathname-open-review.md`.
* **Closed, 2026-09-30 (interactive `full auto` build run; plan session `d4edd5c8-b834-46cd-aec7-058afcc03b66`, implementation session `68d0cce0-18f9-4c4b-8eb8-cf5d43283c6d`; `0e2d799b`, `83ec7fd6`; decision `d-20260930-10`):** on Linux the leaf is opened `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW` relative to the retained parent, verified with `fstat`, and reopened through `/proc/self/fd/<n>` with SQLite's flags minus `O_NOFOLLOW`; every refusal and failure closes only the `O_PATH` descriptor, so no lockable descriptor of an unverified inode is created or closed (measured: an `O_PATH` close leaves the process's POSIX locks intact). On other unix platforms a mismatched descriptor of a live-bound inode and an unclassified (`fstat`-failed) descriptor are never closed; retention is bounded by refusing leaf opens with `EMFILE` (refusal counter unchanged) while any retained set holds `QUARANTINE_ADMISSION_LIMIT`. Windows unchanged (handle-scoped locks). Witnesses: Linux swap-before-verification, swap-before-reopen, `fstat` failure and reopen failure, each red on revert (orchestrator-run: `O_PATH` → `O_RDONLY` reddens three, a name-based reopen reddens the fourth); macOS retention, unclassified-bucket and admission witnesses (the last two process-isolated) observe the lock from a forked child — measured by macOS CI only. The lock-probe helper no longer releases the locks it observes. Remaining: the repository's own `open_current` probes still open and close the leaf lockably (`f-20260929-11`); a FIFO swapped into the non-Linux leaf window can still block the open (`f-20260929-03`, annotated). Review record: `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-29-sqlite-leaf-open-review.md`.

### `pool_parent_swap_keeps_wal_and_shm_in_held_parent_and_unlinks_them_there` fails intermittently on an idle machine

* **ID:** f-20260929-07 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs` test `bound_sqlite_witnesses::pool_parent_swap_keeps_wal_and_shm_in_held_parent_and_unlinks_them_there` (assertion at line 3052, `!sidecar_listing(&swap.held_parent, "pool.db3")…any(-wal|-shm)`), introduced by `9ea21bc0` (2026-09-29).
* **Defect:** measured 2026-09-29 on atlas against the current `master` test binary: run alone with `--exact`, the test failed 5 of 30 serial runs on an otherwise idle machine and 15 of 72 when 24 copies ran at once. The failing assertion is the post-restore expectation that the held parent no longer lists `pool.db3-wal`/`-shm`; the sidecars are sometimes still present when the assertion samples the directory, so either their unlink is asynchronous to the observation (pool connection drop on another thread) or the code under test can leave them behind. It first surfaced as a red `backend-coverage` gate while `backend-test` ran beside it.
* **Why it matters:** an intermittently red backend gate on every push that touches `src-tauri/**`, locally and on CI, and a test that cannot distinguish a real sidecar leak from a timing race — the property it guards (sidecars are unlinked in the held parent) is exactly what `f-20260929-01` promised.
* **Proposed fix:** establish which it is before touching the assertion: trace when the pool's connections holding the WAL/SHM are closed relative to `initialization_connection` returning `Conflict`; if the unlink is legitimately deferred to connection drop, make the test wait on that deterministic event (drop the pool or the repository entry) rather than sampling; if sidecars can survive, fix the code. Prove with 200 serial and 200 concurrent runs green.
* **Found by:** Claude Code, ChessFable push-gate speed investigation 2026-09-29 (concurrent receipt-gate experiment; reproduction loop in that session).

Handled 2026-09-29 in 8b97e423. Mechanism confirmed by close-thread instrumentation (25/240 runs closed SQLite on an r2d2 worker thread): r2d2 `add_connection` holds an upgraded `Arc<SharedPool>` across the connect, so after a probe conflict retired the entry the last pool reference could drop on the worker after the caller returned, closing the idle connection (and unlinking the sidecars) late. Fix in the code, not the test: a per-entry `ConnectionTracker` counts in-flight connects and open handles; retirement refuses new connects, drops the pool and waits until both counts are zero. Before/after with the test run alone: 5/30 → 0/300 serial, 15/72 → 0/600 concurrent (24-way). No assertion changed. Implemented by a Codex write leaf in the push-gate parallelism run; reviewed in that run's push review.

* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/error.rs:378` `map_sqlite_establish`; callers `src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs:514` (`read_revision`) and the pool's establish path via `classify_bound_open_error_result` (`repository.rs:1099`), which passes the original error through when neither the binding's refusal counter nor the authority probe reports a conflict.
* **Defect:** every establish failure that is not `SQLITE_NOTADB` becomes `Error::InvalidInput("could not open SQLite database: …")`, so a host-side failure — `EACCES`, `EMFILE`, `ENOSPC`, an I/O error, or (after `f-20260929-06`) a failed `/proc/self/fd` reopen on Linux — carries the same variant as a malformed database. The SQLite message is appended, but the variant is what callers and the renderer classification (`f-20260830-08`) key on.
* **Why it matters:** the user is told the input is invalid when the file is fine and the host refused the open, and any retry or recovery keyed on the variant treats a transient host failure as permanent bad input.
* **Proposed fix:** map establish failures by SQLite's extended/system error (`sqlite3_system_errno` or the `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`/`SQLITE_IOERR` family) to `Error::Io` for host failures, keep `InvalidInput` for `NOTADB` and malformed-schema cases; check every caller's handling of the two variants before changing it.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-error-handling`, plan review round 1 of the `f-20260929-06` build run, 2026-09-29 (Claude Code orchestrator session d4edd5c8-b834-46cd-aec7-058afcc03b66). Related: `f-20260830-08` (renderer error classification).

Location correction 2026-09-30 (records review): at `3ed94336` the callers are `read_revision` (`src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs` ~590) and `classify_bound_open_error` (~1086), which passes through `classify_bound_open_error_result` (~1178); the line numbers in **Where** above were stale when filed. The defect is unchanged.

## 2026-09-29 — filed through the inbox spool

### Every authority probe of a pooled database opens and closes the leaf, releasing the process's SQLite POSIX locks on it

* **ID:** f-20260929-11 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** sqlite-pathname-open · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs:814` `DatabaseFileTarget::open_current` (returns an `fs::File` of the leaf opened by `open_regular_at`); its production consumers in `src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs` drop that file as an identity probe: `pre_build_probe` / `initial_probe` (~`:775`, `:792`), `pre_get_probe` / `post_get_probe` around every pooled `get()` (~`:961`, `:986`), and the bound-open error classifier `classify_bound_open_error` → `classify_bound_open_error_result` (~`:1011`, `:1099`); `:493` keeps the file for reading.
* **Defect:** SQLite's unix locks are process-associated `fcntl` locks, and closing *any* descriptor of an inode releases every such lock the process holds on it. Measured 2026-09-29 on atlas (kernel 7.0, persistent `F_OFD_GETLK` probe descriptor): a read lock taken through one descriptor is gone after another plain descriptor of the same inode is opened and closed; closing an `O_PATH` descriptor leaves it intact. `open_current` probes run while the database's pool holds live SQLite connections, so each probe silently releases the kernel locks behind SQLite's in-memory lock state — the persistent WAL-mode `SHARED` lock on the database file among them. `d-20260929-04` rejected exactly this shape inside the syscall hooks ("identity checks that open and close the leaf"), but the repository's own probes still do it on every pooled `get()`.
* **Why it matters:** with the `SHARED` lock gone, another process that closes its last connection to the same database obtains `EXCLUSIVE`, checkpoints and unlinks the `-wal`/`-shm` this process is still using (`sqlite3WalClose`), or a rollback-mode writer proceeds under a reader that believes it holds a lock — database corruption. It happens in normal operation whenever a second process (another app instance, an SQLite tool) has the database open, not only under an attack. It also undercuts `f-20260929-06`, whose hook-level fix guarantees the open hook never closes a lockable foreign descriptor while the classifier and the pre/post-get probes then close lockable descriptors of the target itself.
* **Proposed fix:** identity-only probes stop creating lockable descriptors: on Linux open the leaf `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW` (or `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` relative to the verified parent) and compare identity; on macOS use `fstatat` relative to the verified parent; Windows is unaffected (`LockFileEx` locks belong to their handle). Keep `open_current` returning a readable `File` only for consumers that read. Add a witness that holds a SQLite lock through a pooled connection, drives `get()` and the classifier, and asserts the lock survives with a persistent probe descriptor.
* **Open question:** which `open_current` consumers need a readable descriptor rather than identity only, and what identity-only primitive (`O_PATH` descriptor vs `fstatat` on the verified parent) keeps the parent-verification and reparse/wrong-kind classification that `open_current` performs today on every platform?
* **Found by:** Codex `review-correctness`, plan review round 2 of the `f-20260929-06` build run, 2026-09-29 (Claude Code orchestrator session d4edd5c8-b834-46cd-aec7-058afcc03b66); widened by the orchestrator from the classifier to every probe consumer by source reading. Related: `f-20260929-06`, `d-20260929-04`.

Location correction 2026-09-30 (records review): at `3ed94336` the identity-only `open_current` consumers in `src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs` are `entry_probe` (~1015, both attempts; its file becomes `initial_probe` in `entry()` ~819/~847), `pre_build_probe` (~859), the post-build `initial_probe` (~878), `pre_get_probe` (~1051), `post_get_probe` (~1075, returned to the caller and dropped with the connection) and the classifier `classify_bound_open_error` (~1100 → `classify_bound_open_error_result` ~1178). The consumer that keeps the file for reading is `identity_from_probe` (~580), reached from `database_identity` (~488); `:493` in **Where** pointed at that wrapper, not the read. The defect is unchanged.
<!-- ledger-meta {"command":"annotate","effect_lines":1,"effect_sha256":"4d7dfde52275aeeb73ee8ca5bc9e53ef380c995862dcc70d6ab88fb2e347adea","input_sha256":"a136bc97b8ae7e8ec9154394c210111bf9f8e8b773d07c6e417a1748b187f9d9","kind":"mutation-receipt","operation":"acca8ae7c03ffaa44f1bbce4cb185064ce91b180185621a3b844e0bf71ebdc28","options":{"section":null},"request_id_sha256":null,"results":["f-20260929-11"],"target":"f-20260929-11","v":1} -->

* **Closed, 2026-10-01 (drain `full auto` build run, session `91758424-781d-4333-940b-009a6dbfb9d0`; `83118f08`, `bc44f238`, `78766420`, `4c62f32f`; decision `d-20261001-05`):** no `open_current` consumer read bytes, so `DatabaseFileTarget::open_current` became `probe_current`, returning identity, length and full-precision mtime; every consumer named above uses it. On every unix `infra::fs::probe_regular_file_at` creates no leaf descriptor: no-follow `statat` (regular + identity) → `faccessat(R_OK, AT_EACCESS)` (keeps `PermissionDenied` for an unreadable leaf; exactly `AT_EACCESS` because rustix 1.1.4 has no fallback for other flag sets on Linux < 5.8, pinned by a `platform_support` row) → `statat` again, identity and kind must match (else `Conflict`). Windows keeps a read handle (handle-scoped locks). Witnesses: a pooled read transaction's SQLite shared lock survives a second pooled connection, `database_identity` and the bound-open classifier (orchestrator-run: red when the probe opens the leaf again); exact sub-second and pre-epoch mtime; the stat sandwich (symlink and other-inode swaps → `Conflict`); a FIFO leaf → `Conflict` without blocking; the classifier consults its probe with an unchanged refusal count. Known limit: an unobserved symlink swap during the access check changes only which error one probe reports. Remaining elsewhere: lockable descriptors of an inode aliased under another capability kind (puzzle, PGN, sidecar) — filed from this run (inbox `20261001-085423-2254262-1790837663344753656-3`). Review record: `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-01-sqlite-pathname-open-review.md`.
<!-- ledger-meta {"command":"annotate","effect_lines":1,"effect_sha256":"683542a7e86b3d9c5e59d3dcc4180b833048fe37d816d630e5b852f8184bac59","input_sha256":"91d44cac3fa8bcb303cf8bd45c354a8e7ca9e807416f07ec5c3b31bb82740f48","kind":"mutation-receipt","operation":"9cb95865e142e27b045a48b47c778a1ab1f89d1da1eac556d0bfc4225dc1b4e4","options":{"section":null},"request_id_sha256":null,"results":["f-20260929-11"],"target":"f-20260929-11","v":1} -->

* **Precision note, 2026-10-01 (records review of the closing run):** the closure's "exactly `AT_EACCESS`" clause holds on Linux < 5.8 only while the real and effective uid and gid match — rustix 1.1.4 falls back to plain `faccessat` only then (`src/backend/linux_raw/fs/syscalls.rs:1441-1451`) and otherwise returns `ENOSYS`, failing every probe closed. The app is never installed setuid or setgid. The decision is restated with this precondition as `d-20261001-06`, which supersedes `d-20261001-05`.

* **ID:** f-20260929-12 · **Status:** open · **Area:** gate-scripts · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none

A `pnpm mutation:backend` started (by another session or agent) after the guard passed acquires the fence and edits tracked `src-tauri` sources in place while the push gates are still compiling and testing, so a gate can measure mutated code — or record a receipt over it if the mutant is reverted before the receipt's second sample. ## 2026-09-30 — filed through the inbox spool

### LRU eviction drops a database entry without draining its SQLite connections, so one can close after a later delete of the same file

* **ID:** f-20260930-01 · **Status:** open · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs` `evict_idle_entries` (~line 973, called under the repository state lock from `entry()` ~915); `close_retired_entry` (~952) and `DrainGate` (~109) are the drain every other retirement path uses since `3ed94336`.
* **Defect:** eviction removes an idle entry (`Arc::strong_count == 1`, no lease, not retiring) from `RepositoryState.entries` and drops it without closing its connection gate or waiting for outstanding connection tickets. An r2d2 `add_connection` job started by an earlier `get` can still hold an upgraded pool reference and a live or in-flight SQLite handle (the f-20260929-07 mechanism). A later `delete_exclusive_cancellable` of the same file then finds no entry, drains nothing, and unlinks while that handle is still open. The window is small (a replenishment job outliving the `get` that spawned it), reported by the repair leaf of the 2026-09-30 push review.
* **Why it matters:** it is the last retirement path that can close an SQLite handle (and unlink WAL/SHM) after the file was deleted or replaced, which every other path now excludes.
* **Proposed fix:** close the evicted entry's connection gate and drop its pool at eviction without blocking under the state lock, and keep the evicted gates reachable (for example a per-key list of draining gates in `RepositoryState`) so `delete_exclusive_inner` and `entry()` rebuild wait on them through `DrainGate::wait_drained` before unlinking or opening a fresh pool.
* **Open question:** where do evicted-but-draining gates live and who prunes them — a per-key list in `RepositoryState` pruned on drain, or eviction deferred to a path that may block — without holding the state lock across a wait?
* **Found by:** Codex write leaf (repair of the `8b97e423` push review), out-of-scope report; confirmed by the orchestrator from source, 2026-09-30. Related: `f-20260929-07`.

## 2026-09-30 — filed through the inbox spool

### Frontend tests that call `vi.resetModules()` and dynamically import a large module graph pay its cold transform inside their first timed test, which crosses Vitest's 5 s default when many workers run under load

* **ID:** f-20260930-02 · **Status:** open · **Area:** frontend-ui · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** test files that reset modules and then `await import(...)` app modules inside a test body — candidates from `grep -l vi.resetModules src`: `src/index.test.tsx`, `src/components/home/Accounts.test.tsx`, `src/i18n.test.ts`, `src/components/databases/FideInfo.test.tsx`, `src/state/pathOwners.test.ts`, `src/state/store/tabStorage.test.ts`, `src/state/atoms.lifecycle.test.ts`, `src/state/workspace.test.ts` (`src/utils/sound.test.ts` is fixed, see below).
* **Defect:** Vitest transforms a module on first import through one transform server in the main process. A test file whose first test dynamically imports a large graph (e.g. `@/state/atoms`) pays that cold transform inside the test handler, where `testTimeout` (5 s) applies. Since the push gate sizes Vitest workers from the memory budget (`d-20260930-03`, 22 workers on atlas), up to 22 files request transforms at once and queue; under load from other sessions the first test of `src/utils/sound.test.ts` took 5047 ms (2.10 s alone) in `pnpm gate:ensure frontend-coverage` on 2026-09-30, load average 45-65, and its sibling then failed on the leaked call.
* **Fix pattern (precedent):** `d-20260901-36` option (b) — static top-level side-effect imports of the modules the tests import dynamically, so the transform is paid at collection, which `testTimeout` does not cover; `vi.resetModules()` keeps per-test module freshness. Applied to `src/utils/sound.test.ts` in the push-gate parallelism run. Never raise `testTimeout`.
* **Open question (lens tier):** which of the candidate files actually import a heavy graph in their first timed test (measure each file alone: first-test duration vs. the rest), and whether a shared warm-up belongs in a Vitest `setupFiles` entry instead of per-file imports.
* **Why it matters:** a push gate that fails when the machine is busy teaches re-running instead of looking (the failure `f-20260917-11` recorded), and every such file is one more source of a red receipt gate that is not about the diff.
* **Related:** `f-20260920-13` (an order-dependent frontend test, different cause), `d-20260901-36`, `d-20260930-03`.
* **Found by:** Claude Code (Opus 5.5), final `frontend-coverage` gate of the push-gate parallelism build run (session a3a230ef-7b5b-4be0-82ec-2e5fb8953292), 2026-09-30.
* **Mitigated, still open (2026-09-30, same run):** `src/utils/sound.test.ts` now warms its imports statically (70f8a90b); then the gate hit the same class in `src/index.test.tsx` (5040 ms) and `src/chessground/Chessground.test.tsx` (5110 ms). A measured sweep of all 16 files with `await import(` in test bodies found seven whose first dynamic import costs 0.29-0.76 s alone and none where a static warm-up is safe: `index.tsx` starts the app at import; `state/atoms` (reached by Chessground, Accounts, engineOwnerStorage, atoms.lifecycle) snapshots and repairs storage and removes `document-dir` at module scope; `pathOwners` snapshots storage at module scope behind a spy the test installs first; FideInfo `vi.doMock`s its flag module. The gate is now protected by Vitest's persistent transform cache (d-20260930-07, commit after 98e0a6c0): warm, those first tests take ~0.26 s. What remains is the design question: move storage snapshot/repair and app start-up out of module evaluation (an explicit init), so tests can import these modules without side effects and a cold cache cannot put a transform inside a timed test.
<!-- ledger-meta {"command":"annotate","effect_lines":1,"effect_sha256":"20ce864cfa580efe7b7054287eb4d76ea44aab1bfa73543ce7483517ddc4280b","input_sha256":"549585ad3c335b635bab7e8396d2c20989ce90b2f2428c8e311487518e315f25","kind":"mutation-receipt","operation":"8df3bf365b8f077757c748029af19d5ae77df90b6c8a100ca93138a317c7e00b","options":{"section":null},"request_id_sha256":null,"results":["f-20260930-02"],"target":"f-20260930-02","v":1} -->

* **Residual deferred here (2026-09-30, review of 4554d0c3, `review-root-cause` blocker, confidence 99):** the transform cache only helps once warm. A cold cache — the first gate run after a lockfile change, or any CI job (CI does not keep `node_modules/.experimental-vitest-cache`) — still pays the transform inside these first tests. Measured: cold at 22 workers without outside load they take 2.3-2.4 s (index, Chessground); the three 5 s timeouts happened only under outside load average 45-65. CI runs 4 workers exactly as before this run and these tests never timed out there. Removing the residual is this finding's design question (side-effect-free module evaluation), not a cache or timeout setting.
<!-- ledger-meta {"command":"annotate","effect_lines":1,"effect_sha256":"2c28d967b863dc9b264ecb15e015469d9c14d3b0eb214f8997862680d6245532","input_sha256":"3a225cf4f8ed549d1b9d92254baa056872aabd23c29a1199ad1506862a07202b","kind":"mutation-receipt","operation":"a51b0b3ffc6677af0ca08d5712257d5c1602901733642e6c7b2e532268859c79","options":{"section":null},"request_id_sha256":null,"results":["f-20260930-02"],"target":"f-20260930-02","v":1} -->

* **Open question, restated (2026-09-30):** the entry's original question (which files, and per-file warm imports vs. a setup file) is answered by the sweep annotated above: static warm-ups are unsafe in every affected file except `sound.test.ts`. What remains open is only the design question — move storage snapshot/repair, `document-dir` cleanup and app start-up out of module evaluation (an explicit init called by the app and by each test), so these modules can be imported without side effects and a cold transform cache cannot put a transform inside a timed test. Decision in force: d-20260930-09.

### Push gates still run inside the 8G agent session scope; wrap them in tuxedo-config's agent-gate

* **ID:** f-20260930-03 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** gate-scripts · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `.claude/skills/push/SKILL.md` gate entry (`pnpm gates:push -- <blocks>`, ~59-67) and standalone receipt gate invocations; `scripts/gate-parallelism.mjs` (cgroup `memory.max` sizing).
* **Defect:** measured 2026-09-29 (tuxedo-config f-20260929-01): Stryker was cgroup-OOM-killed in the 8G session `run-*.scope` at 12, 18 and 23 runners, and four concurrent receipt gates peaked at 6.06 GB there. tuxedo-config (commit dc95d84, f-20260929-01) now provides `agent-gate <command>`, which from a capped session starts the command in `agents.slice/agent-gate-*.scope` bound to the session, capped at 70 % of the slice's `MemoryHigh` (tower 28 GiB), `OOMPolicy=stop`, falling back to in-place execution with a warning.
* **Why it matters:** `gate-parallelism.mjs` already sizes workers from its own cgroup's `memory.max`; inside a gate scope it reads 28 GiB instead of 8 GiB, so the push gates can use the cores without being OOM-killed.
* **Change:** run the gate scheduler as `if command -v agent-gate >/dev/null 2>&1; then agent-gate pnpm gates:push -- …; else pnpm gates:push -- …; fi` (availability only, never exit status), and the same for standalone receipt gates the skill routes; re-measure Stryker's runner count inside the gate scope.

Converge here by running the whole heavy gate as `agent-gate <gate command>` with no `command -v` fallback, size per-step workers under rule (b) inside that one scope, and retire `scripts/heavy-gate.sh` and its vendored lock snippet once the strict launcher has landed; until then the repository's existing compliant route stays, and today's `agent-gate` alone meets neither (a) nor (c). Contract: `~/.claude/references/gate-performance.md` (c).

### `SearchIndexIdentity::for_database` and `SearchCache::invalidate_entries` reach the filesystem by pathname in `main.rs`

* **ID:** f-20261001-01 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/main.rs` — `SearchIndexIdentity::for_database` (`database.canonicalize()`, `preferred_index.exists()`, `legacy.exists()`, `index.canonicalize()`, `index.metadata()`) and the search cache's `invalidate_entries` (`database.canonicalize()`); callers `src-tauri/src/db/search.rs` (`SearchIndexIdentity::for_database(database, expected_source)`, `search_cache.invalidate_database(...)`), `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs` (`invalidate_database(path)` / `invalidate_database(target.path())`), `src-tauri/src/db/search_index.rs`.
* **Defect:** these six calls are the only production `std::path::Path` pathname reaches outside `src-tauri/src/infra/` on Linux, measured 2026-10-01 at d7fd20e5 with `cargo clippy --bins` under a `disallowed-methods` list of the ten `Path` filesystem methods (seven hits: these six plus one in `infra/path_authority/mod.rs`, which is sanctioned). The native-fs convention (`d-20260901-02`, `d-20260901-03`) keeps production filesystem reach inside `infra/`, and `main.rs` already left the shrink-only R3 allowlist, so it cannot be re-added there. `f-20260912-03`'s plan makes these calls visible to the gate and holds them under a shrink-only baseline of statement-level `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)]` attributes in `main.rs`; this finding owns emptying that baseline.
* **Why it matters:** the identity of a cached search index is computed from pathname resolution (`canonicalize` follows every symlink, `exists` then `metadata` is a check-then-use pair), while the database itself is already bound through `DatabaseFileTarget` (`d-20260912-04`..`-06`). An index replaced between the existence probe and the stat, or a symlinked sidecar, yields an identity that does not describe the file later mapped.
* **Open question:** what identity does a search-index cache key hold without pathname resolution — the `DatabaseFileTarget`'s canonical binding plus a descriptor-relative stat of the chosen sidecar (preferred vs legacy) through `infra/`, or a new `infra` helper that returns the chosen sidecar with its identity from one held parent descriptor — and do `invalidate_database` callers that still pass a raw `&Path` (`db/mod.rs`) need a target first?
* **Done when:** no `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)]` remains in `main.rs` and the shrink-only baseline entry for `main.rs` in `scripts/check-rust-release-surface.mjs` is removed.
* **Related:** `f-20260912-03` (the gate that counts these calls; it carries no `Root`), `f-20260912-11` / `f-20260912-12` (handled; moved the `db/search.rs` `canonicalize()` sites onto `target.path()`), `d-20260912-09`.
* **Found by:** Claude Code, PLAN-ONLY planner for `f-20260912-03`, drain session e5262241-8afd-456c-8e90-e42ef8b83982, 2026-10-01.
* **Handled (2026-10-08, Codex drain):** Implementation `9247edf2` removes the six production pathname reaches, every statement-level disallowed-method expectation, and both R5 baseline entries. SearchIndexIdentity stamps the exact opened preferred-sidecar descriptor and carries the authority target's database binding. Invalidation takes DatabaseFileTarget and evicts by matching database path or object. Stamp errors propagate without legacy fallback or cache publication. The database probe remains the linearization point and cancellation/invalidation still control publication.
* **Proof:** Root independently ran cargo fmt, Linux all-target clippy, `pnpm rust:windows:check`, unfiltered `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --bin chessfable` (2,079 passed, two ignored), all 298 release-surface checker tests, `pnpm gates:contract:check`, the disallowed-method grep (only crate-root test allowance), and `pnpm checks:pre-review`. Five documented Git-derived or selective-withdrawal witnesses failed at the intended runtime assertions and passed after byte-for-byte restoration. Windows and macOS runtime evidence is required from pushed-head CI before this run completes.
* **Decisions and limits:** d-20261008-15, d-20261008-16 and d-20261008-17 record descriptor identity, error propagation and empty shrink-only baselines. The permission-stat fallback question is dissolved because identity no longer selects a sidecar by pathname. Successor f-20261008-07 owns the combined changed-object plus changed-spelling limitation and inherited R1-01. Load `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-08-f-20260927-07-review.md` for the complete review history and proof evidence. Loader deduplication f-20260914-04 remains outside this migration.

### A database inode authorized under a second capability kind can be opened and closed lockably while a game-database pool holds SQLite locks on it

* **ID:** f-20261001-02 · **Status:** open · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/resolved.rs` (~544, ~556, ~860: the generic resolver opens and retains an ordinary leaf descriptor in `ResolvedPath.file`); its consumers `src-tauri/src/puzzle.rs` (~103, ~123, ~160, ~188, ~213 puzzle reads through `schema_specific_connection_expected_file_cancellable`, which also `try_clone()`s the descriptor; ~610 puzzle deletion), `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs` (~3123, an existing `WritePgn` export destination resolved and held through export), and the search-index sidecar reads `src-tauri/src/db/search.rs` (~335) and `src-tauri/src/db/search_index.rs` (~886).
* **Defect:** SQLite's unix locks are process-associated `fcntl` locks, and closing any ordinary descriptor of an inode releases every such lock the process holds on it (measured 2026-09-29 on atlas, recorded in `f-20260929-11` and `d-20260930-10`). Game-database pools are keyed by `DatabaseFileTarget`, but nothing stops the same inode from also being authorized as a puzzle database, a PGN import/export file or a search-index sidecar (a user pick of the same file, or a hard link). Each of those capabilities opens an ordinary descriptor on the leaf and closes it when the operation ends, possibly while a game-database pool on that inode holds a live SQLite lock — the same lock-release hazard `f-20260929-11` removes from the repository's own probes. Found by a locate probe of the `f-20260929-11` build run (2026-10-01), which classified these sites as "lockable open+close while pooled possible" only through such a cross-capability alias.
* **Why it matters:** with the lock silently gone, another process can checkpoint and unlink the `-wal`/`-shm` this process still uses, or write under a reader that believes it holds a lock — database corruption. Reachable only when one inode is authorized under two capability kinds, so far rarer than `f-20260929-11`.
* **Open question:** should path authority refuse (or a capability consumer detect) an inode that is live in a game-database pool when it is resolved under another capability kind — and if so, where is the cross-kind inode registry and what does the user see — or should each of these consumers stop holding an ordinary descriptor (identity by `fstatat` / `O_PATH`, snapshot copy through a non-lockable route), given that a puzzle snapshot and a PGN export genuinely read or write the bytes?
* **Related:** `f-20260929-11` (the repository's own probes; this finding is the residual outside the repository), `d-20260930-10`, `d-20260929-05` (cross-directory hard-link refusal for game databases only).

### Threat mode's `swapMove` keeps the en-passant square and can put the side not to move in check

* **ID:** f-20261001-03 · **Status:** open · **Area:** chess-tree · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/utils/chessops.ts:36-45` (`swapMove`), callers `src/components/boards/EvalListener.tsx:109,273`, `src/components/panels/analysis/BestMoves.tsx:142,330`, `src/components/common/DetachedEval.tsx:97`.
* **Defect:** `swapMove` flips only `setup.turn`. An en-passant square that was legal for the original side to move is kept for the other side (an ep square on the wrong rank), and a position whose side to move is in check becomes one where the side not to move is in check. The backend's shakmaty validation rejects both, so threat mode shows an error toast instead of a threat line.
* **Why it matters:** threat analysis fails in ordinary positions right after a double pawn push or a check.
* **Found by:** Claude Code (Opus 5.5) Stockfish 19 upgrade planning run, GUI-side UCI audit leaf, confirmed by the orchestrator reading `swapMove`, 2026-10-01.

### A catalog engine install is never persisted: the record carries catalog-only keys that strict owner validation refuses

* **ID:** f-20261001-06 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-state · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/utils/engines.ts:331-346` (`installDefaultEngine` returns `{...engine, …}`), `src/state/engineOwnerStorage.ts:96-103,173-178` (`inspectEngineOwnerValue` requires `equal(value, parsed.data)`), `src/components/engines/AddEngine.tsx:224-230` (receipt ignored).
* **Defect:** the installed record keeps the manifest keys `path`, `sha256`, `signature`, `os`, `bmi2`, `image` and `imageUrl`. Zod strips them on parse, so the strict equality fails and `enqueueEngineOwnerSave` returns `saved:false` ("refusing to persist an invalid engine owner record"). Jotai already holds the new list in memory, so the card says "Installed"; every later `engines` save in that session is refused as well (the invalid entry stays in the list), and after a restart only the old engines remain while the new handle is pruned. Measured 2026-10-01 with a scratch vitest against the real `inspectEngineOwnerValue`: the install-shaped record yields `null`, the same record without those keys yields `{"capabilityIds":["h"],"attachmentIds":[]}`. Existing `AddEngine` tests mock the save and cannot see it.
* **Why it matters:** the default-engine catalog (including Stockfish 19) cannot be used at all; the failure is silent.
* **Planned:** obligation O2 of `tasks/plans/2026-10-01-stockfish-19-upgrade.md` (schema-exact record from one shared install function; `AddEngine` honours the receipt).
* **Found by:** Claude Code (Opus 5.5) Stockfish 19 upgrade planning run, research leaf confirmed by the orchestrator's own probe run, 2026-10-01.
* **Correction (2026-10-01, `$push` records review of the sidebar active-marker push):** "every later `engines` save in that session is refused as well" is too broad. Later saves are refused only while the invalid entry is still in the list; removing that engine on the Engines page filters it out (`src/components/engines/EnginesPage.tsx:682`, `setEngines(... .filter((e) => e.id !== engine.id))`), after which the remaining valid list can be saved again.

### Engine termination is not surfaced: analysis spins forever, the engine's last `info string` reason is lost, and a game blames the engine with "Abandonment"

* **ID:** f-20261001-07 · **Status:** open · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/engine/process.rs:486` (exit status discarded), `:2574-2576` (actor log), `src-tauri/src/chess.rs:315,593` (`info string` during a search read as "no moves"), `:633-641` (supervisor entry removed, Logs panel empty), `src/components/panels/analysis/BestMoves.tsx:248-305,369-371` (loading skeleton and progress bar stay), `src/components/boards/EvalListener.tsx:415-418` (generic toast), `src-tauri/src/game.rs:2969-2984` (engine side loses by "Abandonment").
* **Defect:** when an engine process exits mid-session, the renderer gets only the fixed "Engine disconnected" text; the analysis panel stays in its loading state indefinitely, the engine's final line (Stockfish 19 prints `info string CRITICAL ERROR: Command … failed. Reason: …` before `exit(1)`) is unreachable from the Logs panel, and a game charges the loss to the engine even when the GUI sent the bad input.
* **Open question:** what owns the final word of a terminated engine — a typed `EngineTerminated { reason }` error carrying the last `info string`/stderr line through the facade, or a retained bounded post-mortem log the Logs panel can still read after the supervisor entry is removed — and what the analysis panel shows instead of the skeleton (error state with retry), and whether a game should end as an engine failure rather than "Abandonment".
* **Why it matters:** any engine crash (SF18 segfaults on some FENs; SF19 terminates on strict-validation failures) leaves the user with a spinner and no reason. The Stockfish 19 upgrade plan removes every known ChessFable input that triggers SF19 termination, so this is the same hazard as before the upgrade, not a regression of it.
* **Found by:** Claude Code (Opus 5.5) Stockfish 19 upgrade planning run, GUI-side UCI audit leaf, 2026-10-01. Related plan: `tasks/plans/2026-10-01-stockfish-19-upgrade.md` (Not part of this task).

### Opening a database, a database game or a game inside a PGN file has no visible affordance — only double-clicks and unlabelled icons

* **ID:** f-20261001-08 · **Status:** open · **Area:** frontend-ui · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/components/databases/DatabasesPage.tsx` (~274: a database card opens only on `onDoubleClick`; a single click selects it and shows the details panel whose `Databases.Settings.Explore` button is the only labelled route), `src/components/databases/GameTable.tsx` (~221: a game opens in an analysis tab only on `onRowDoubleClick`; ~310: a single click only fills the preview), `src/components/databases/GameCard.tsx` (~41: the icon-only "Analyze game" action), `src/components/files/FileCard.tsx` (~94: the icon-only `Common.Open` magnifier is the only way to open the selected game), `src/components/panels/info/GameSelector.tsx` (~179: a row has `onClick` → `setPage` only, no double-click).

On the Databases page a single click on "Meine Partien" appears to do nothing useful; in the Files page he double-clicked a game in the file card's game list, which only selects it, and the open action is a bare magnifier icon with a tooltip. The two lists that show games also disagree: a database game row opens on double-click, a PGN game row does not. The double-click on a file *row in the tree* works (`f-20260905-14`); this is about the database card, the game rows and the icon-only open actions.

* **Open question:** which single open interaction (labelled button, single click, double-click/Enter) every game list and the database card share, and where the shared open-game affordance lives so the database table and the file game list stop being wired separately.
* **Why `build`:** interaction design across two pages and three components with a shared affordance to extract; needs a plan.
* **Related:** `f-20260905-14` (handled: tree double-click and the restored file card), the Files/Databases library question filed in the same session, the database preview layout finding filed in the same session.
* **Found by:** Felix exploring his imported games and repertoires, session e3bd1021-4d34-443f-96c0-a1af650f0984, 2026-10-01 (screenshots in the session).

### The database Games view splits list and preview 50/50 with no resize, so the preview board can never be larger than a quarter of the window width

* **ID:** f-20261001-09 · **Status:** open · **Area:** frontend-ui · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/components/databases/GridLayout.tsx` (`<Group grow>` with two equal columns, no splitter), `src/components/databases/GamePreview.tsx:60` (`boardSide = min(frameHeight, frameWidth / 2)` when controls are shown, so the board takes at most half of the preview column), used by `GameTable.tsx`, `PlayerTable.tsx`, `TournamentTable.tsx`.
* **Defect:** Felix (2026-10-01, 2000px-wide window) wanted a bigger board while browsing "Meine Partien" and found no way to enlarge it: the table and the preview are fixed halves and the board is capped at half of its half. The analysis tab already offers resizable panes (`BoardsPage.tsx`, `react-mosaic-component`), so the database view is the odd one out.
* **Fix shape:** a draggable divider between table and preview (persisted width, bounded min/max), and a preview layout that lets the board grow into available height (stack notation under the board when the column is tall rather than always beside it). Reuse whatever splitter primitive the app already ships rather than adding a second one. Pixels via `pnpm test:e2e:container`; check the 320px / 200% font-scale case (`f-20260829-02`).
* **Open question:** which splitter primitive the database view adopts (reuse of the analysis tab's mosaic or a lighter divider), how its width is persisted, and how the preview arranges board and notation when the column is tall versus wide.

Olvidé…` starts with "number + period + space", which Markdown parses as an ordered list starting at 59, rendering a block-level list with margins and an empty gap; ChessBase/PGN comments are plain text, so any comment opening with `12. `, `- `, `# ` or `> ` is restyled; (2) because each comment ends the row, a game where nearly every move has a short comment collapses to one half-move per line and wastes most of the panel width.

### Games are split across a Files page and a Databases page by storage format, not by what the games are for

* **ID:** f-20261001-11 · **Status:** open · **Area:** frontend-ui · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** the sidebar routes to `src/components/files/FilesPage.tsx` (PGN files in the workspace folder, typed game/repertoire/tournament/puzzle/other via `src/components/files/file.ts`) and `src/components/databases/DatabasesPage.tsx` (SQLite `.db3` collections built by `convert_pgn`, `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs:727`; Lichess/Chess.com account sync always writes a database, `src/components/home/AccountCard.tsx:156`).
* **Observation:** Felix (2026-10-01) asked why his own played games ("Meine Partien", 116 games) live under Databases while his opening files live under Files: "in chess space this is all in one list. This is all the same structure. Whether I use my games or an opening preparation." The split is inherited from En Croissant. Technically it is justified — PGN files are editable documents (variations, comments, repertoire practice), databases are indexed copies for position search, player/tournament views, deduplication and the opening-explorer reference — but the UI exposes the storage format as two top-level places, and a user thinks in purposes ("my games", "my Caro-Kann prep").
* **Open question:** how a single library list composes the database detail pane and the file card, and what happens to the two existing routes, once Felix chooses an option below.
* **Decision:** Should ChessFable show one library of everything that holds games — databases and PGN files in a single list, each with a type badge and the actions that fit it — instead of two separate sidebar pages?
  * **(a) One library view.** One sidebar entry; one searchable list with type badges (Games database / Repertoire / Study / Tournament / Puzzle); selecting an item shows the matching detail pane (database stats + Explore, or the file card); storage stays exactly as it is (PGN files stay files, `.db3` stays SQLite) and "Add" offers both "import as database" and "create file". Costs: a new page that composes both existing panes, one merged search/filter, and the two old routes kept as redirects; every Files/Databases e2e snapshot changes.
  * **(b) Keep two pages, explain them.** Rename to purpose-based labels (e.g. "Studies & repertoires" / "Game collections"), add a one-line description on each page and cross-links. Costs: cheap; the split itself stays, so "my games" vs "my prep" still means knowing which format each was imported as.
  * **(c) Keep as is.** No cost; the confusion Felix hit stays for every user.
  * **Ruled out:** converting everything to one storage format. Turning repertoires into databases loses free-form editing and the repertoire practice mode; turning databases into PGN loses indexed position search and the opening explorer over large collections (Mega Database). The formats are right; only the presentation is in question.
  * **Recommend:** (a), because it matches how chess players organise material (ChessBase shows one database window for games and openings, Lichess one study list) and removes the "where did my games go" question at its source, while keeping both technically correct storage formats. Against it: it is the largest of the three, it diverges further from upstream En Croissant's navigation (harder to compare against upstream history), and the two detail panes have quite different actions, so a merged list must make clear why a database row offers "Explore" and a file row offers "Open/Practice".
  * **Product impact:** changes where a user finds and opens their games and repertoires — one place instead of two sidebar pages — and what the sidebar shows.
  * **Session:** e3bd1021-4d34-443f-96c0-a1af650f0984 — transcript
    `~/.claude/projects/*/e3bd1021-4d34-443f-96c0-a1af650f0984.jsonl`
* **Decision made:** (a) one library view, as phase 1 of 'one library + linked collections': one Library sidebar entry replacing Files and Databases, one searchable list of files and databases with type badges, detail pane by item type, /files and /databases redirect; phase 2 (every collection exists once, the PGN file is the truth, linked search index) is filed as its own finding — Felix: in chess space this is all in one list; users think in purposes, not storage formats. Chosen 2026-10-04 after the recommendation was reviewed and approved by the orchestrator and four Codex lenses (review-plan, review-root-cause, review-minimalism, review-pgn-index) over four rounds.

### The renderer's tree keeps only 26 glyphs, so ChessBase's `$8` (□) and `$11` (=) render as an empty grey badge and are deleted on the next save

* **ID:** f-20261001-12 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** chess-tree · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/utils/chess.ts:451` (`node.annotations.push(NAG_INFO.get(token.value) || "")` — every NAG outside `NAG_INFO` becomes `""`), `src/utils/chess.ts:452` (the sort puts `""`, nag 0, first), `src/utils/chess.ts:79` (`if (annotation === "") continue;` — the writer drops it), `src/utils/annotation.ts:40` (`NAG_INFO` maps `$7`→□ and `$10`→= but not `$8` or `$11`), `src/components/boards/Board.tsx:473` + `AnnotationHint.tsx` (the board badge draws `annotations[0]`; `""` has colour gray and an empty glyph), `src/state/store/tabStorage.ts:30` (the persisted schema is the same 26-value enum).
* **Defect:** Felix's ChessBase-exported repertoire files (`~/Documents/Sport/Schach/ChessFable/Repertoire/*.pgn`) contain `$8` 2,021 times and `$11` 380 times (all other NAGs in them are understood: `$1 $2 $5 $6 $14 $15 $16 $17 $18 $19`). (1) A move carrying `$8` or `$11` shows a grey dot with no symbol in the corner of its destination square (observed 2026-10-01 on `7. d4 $8` in `Weiß_Königsgambit.pgn`). (2) Saving the game back — to the PGN file or to a database through `write_db_game` — writes the renderer's PGN, which omits every `""`, so every `$8`/`$11` in the saved game is deleted without warning. (3) Because `""` sorts first, a move with both an unknown and a known NAG shows the grey dot instead of the known symbol. The database itself stores NAGs losslessly as raw `$n` strings (`src-tauri/src/db/encoding.rs`, `encode_nag`), so the loss is entirely in the renderer's tree model.
* **Open question:** how the tree stores NAGs losslessly (raw NAG numbers versus glyph aliases), how the Annotate panel's toggles treat alias NAGs (`$7`/`$8` both □, `$10`/`$11` both =), what an unknown NAG shows, and how open tabs persisted in the old 26-glyph shape migrate.
* **Why `build`:** the fix changes the tree node's annotation type, its persisted schema and every consumer; Felix asked for a Codex plan review before implementation.
* **Found by:** Felix noticing the grey dot on 7.d4, session e3bd1021-4d34-443f-96c0-a1af650f0984, 2026-10-01.
* **Handled, 2026-10-03:** The renderer's tree stores raw NAG codes (`TreeNode.nags: number[]`, 0–255, insertion order, duplicates kept) instead of 26 glyphs. One catalogue maps codes to glyphs (`$8` → □ and `$11` → = added), and one projection, `nagGlyphs`, feeds every display consumer, so a code without a glyph draws nothing and never displaces a known symbol. The PGN writer emits every code in ascending order, with a suffix glyph only for a first code of 1–6 (`[1, 2]` → `e4! $2`). Annotate toggles and `goToAnnotation` work on glyph classes. Tabs persisted in the old shape migrate in place without a version bump; invalid, corrupt or over-long legacy arrays keep the unreadable path. Known limit: a tab opened before the fix already lost `$8`/`$11` (and collapsed aliases such as `$23` → `$22`), so such tabs must be reopened from their file before saving. Decisions `d-20261003-15` through `d-20261003-19`. Commits `a6348c79` (implementation), `2f4dc8c4`, `3de938da`, `db20b0ec`, `fb69f852` (diff-review repairs and verify:app staging record). Real window: `pnpm verify:app` NAG scenario green, each of its nine assertions staged red. Display follow-up: `f-20261003-03`. Review: `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-01-lossless-nags-review.md`.

### The persisted `database-view` store hydrates `database` without validation, so a malformed stored handle crashes the database view instead of falling back to the overview

* **ID:** f-20261001-13 · **Status:** open · **Area:** frontend-state · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/state/store/database.ts` (`persist` options `name: "database-view"`, `storage: createJSONStorage(() => sessionStorage)`, ~201-204: no `version`, `migrate` or `merge`); consumers `src/components/databases/databaseRoute.ts` (`sameDatabaseHandle(database.file, active?.file)`), `src/utils/pathCapabilities.ts` (`capabilityKey`, `pathRefKey`: `handle.id` dereference).
* **Defect:** read on HEAD `62c627b8`: the persist middleware restores `state.database` exactly as JSON-parsed. A stored `database` that is JSON-valid but not a `SuccessDatabaseInfo` (e.g. `{}` or `{ "file": {} }`, an older shape, or a hand-edited entry) reaches `capabilityKey(undefined)` / `pathRefKey(undefined)` and throws `TypeError` while rendering `DatabaseView` (via `resolveDatabaseRoute` → `sameDatabaseHandle` → `databaseHandleKey`). Whether WebKitGTK's sessionStorage survives an app restart (which would make an upgrade-time shape change reachable) was not measured.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md` — "Persist only versioned, schema-validated user state and reconcile it against native state at startup." One bad entry turns the database page into a render crash rather than the overview.
* **Change:** validate the hydrated `database` at the store boundary (persist `merge`/`migrate` with a shape check of `type === "success"` and a handle whose key is a non-empty string; drop it otherwise), so every consumer can trust it; prove with a test that seeds `sessionStorage["database-view"]` with a malformed `database` and asserts the store hydrates with `database: undefined`.
* **Context:** surfaced by the `review-persisted-state` lens on the 2026-10-01 database Back-button plan (`tasks/plans/2026-10-01-database-back-button.md`, issue R1-I1). That plan keeps its own sidebar resume link from widening the crash to every page; the pre-existing view/route crash is this finding.
* **Found by:** Claude Code, database Back-button plan review, 2026-10-01.

### A failed engine termination drops the actor from the supervisor, so no later owner can retry or confirm cleanup

* **ID:** f-20261001-14 · **Status:** open · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/engine/process.rs:1448-1461` (`terminate_exact`: `let result = current.actor.terminate().await; self.actors.remove(key); result`), used by `retire_engine`, `retire_executables`, `kill_engine`, `kill_engines` and tab termination.
* **Defect:** when `actor.terminate()` returns an error, the actor is removed from the registry anyway. The child process may still be alive (kill-on-drop is best effort), and nothing — tab close, app shutdown via `RunEvent::ExitRequested`, a later retirement — can find it again.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md` requires cleanup on every exit path; an engine with a large hash (8 GB in Felix's configuration) can outlive its owner unseen.
* **Open question:** keep failed actors in a bounded "reaping" set that shutdown and later retirements retry, or make termination escalate (kill, wait with deadline) until it is confirmed before removal — and how the renderer learns that a process could not be confirmed dead.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-engine-protocol` lens, round 2 of the Stockfish 19 upgrade plan review (`tasks/plans/2026-10-01-stockfish-19-upgrade.md`, issue R2 retirement-failure), confirmed by the orchestrator from source, 2026-10-01.
* **Additional review evidence (2026-10-09):** f-20260926-07 cumulative review traced the normally joined production game loop. src-tauri/src/game.rs logs a terminate_game_engines failure at the loop tail and returns (). Shared pending teardown subsequently removes the failed generation, so finish_retired's unconditional exact termination finds no registered or pending owner and returns Ok. This can make replacement and shutdown_all report success after an unconfirmed reap. Existing clean-join failure tests use a loop that skips engine cleanup and do not exercise that production loss path. The cause is this finding's failed-actor/result retention contract, not an empty-join cancellation gap. Preserve the completed outcome or failed generation until the owning game/shutdown path has observed failure. Verification for this finding must include the production-loop cleanup path, not only direct fallback teardown. The separate design question remains open at build tier. review-error-handling confidence 95, adopting drain a51461c5-317b-40c0-8297-ab16a2fc6904.

### Engine archive staging reopens the destination parent by pathname

* **ID:** f-20261001-15 · **Status:** open · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/fs.rs:1319-1329` (`download_engine_archive_core`: `destination_parent = resolved.target().parent().to_path_buf()`, then `private_tempdir_in(".archive", &destination_parent)`).
* **Defect:** the staging directory is created under a pathname derived from the resolved destination rather than through the verified directory descriptor. If the engine root is renamed and its path replaced by a symlink between resolution and `private_tempdir_in`, download and extraction write staging data under the symlink target; the later atomic install refuses publication, but only after those out-of-authority writes happened.
* **Why it matters:** every other path-authority write door binds to a verified inode; this one is a pathname re-open in the same class the path-authority work closed elsewhere. Reaching it needs a local actor racing the rename, so it is outside accidental-input threat models.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-tauri-security` lens, round 2 of the Stockfish 19 upgrade plan review, 2026-10-01; confirmed by the orchestrator reading `fs.rs:1319-1329`.
